title: Event-driven wake for SDLC skill's monitor loop (host-side)
summary: Architecture design for a new MCP tool `wait_for_status_change(task_id, wait=25, since=...)` that composes the existing EventBus (phase/decision/terminal events) with the existing message_store.get_messages long-poll (OVERSEER_ALERT, CONSENSUS_*) to return immediately when a pipeline-relevant event lands and otherwise fall through with a minimal no-change envelope. `get_status` is unchanged. The SDLC skill's Phase 3 and Phase S5 monitor loops replace `get_status(task_id, wait=25)` with `wait_for_status_change(task_id, wait=25, since=<last_event_id>)`, branching on `changed: true|false` to skip the 10-message `recent_messages` fetch and dashboard re-render on timeout. All seven refine-phase HITL decisions are encoded directly into the design.

problem_statement.description: The SDLC skill's Phase 3 and Phase S5 monitor loops call `get_status(task_id, wait=25)` every iteration (skills/sdlc/SKILL.md:317-319 and skills/sdlc/SKILL.md:1186-1188). The server implementation is a blind `asyncio.sleep(min(wait, 25))` (orchestrator/mcp_server.py:50-67, `_apply_get_status_wait`) — it always sleeps the full 25s even when nothing on the pipeline changed. Every wake re-renders the dashboard, re-classifies messages, and re-evaluates consensus, burning tokens during quiet phases (long `make test` runs, idle BRC consensus, large-diff reviews). It also delays the host's reaction to user-relevant events (OVERSEER_ALERT, HITL gates, phase transitions, terminal state) by up to 25s. Server-side event primitives already exist — message_store.get_messages(wait_for_types=..., from_tip=True) from issue #1919 + #1925 and EventBus pub/sub emitting PHASE_STARTED/PHASE_COMPLETED/PIPELINE_COMPLETED/PIPELINE_FAILED/DECISION_CREATED from orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py:513-553 — but the host-side MCP path does not use them. Issue #1932 is the host-side counterpart to the in-sandbox event-driven waits that #1919 already shipped.
goals: Replace the host monitor loop's blind 25s sleep with an event-triggered wake that returns immediately on any of: OVERSEER_ALERT | CONSENSUS_CONFIRMED | CONSENSUS_NACK | CONSENSUS_RE_REVIEW messages; PHASE_STARTED | PHASE_COMPLETED | PIPELINE_COMPLETED | PIPELINE_FAILED | DECISION_CREATED EventBus events.
Keep the 25s per-call cap parameterized so the eventual upstream fix of anthropics/claude-code#20335 is a one-line change, not a redesign.
Do NOT regress any non-SDLC caller of `get_status` — the new behavior lives in a sibling tool (HITL decision-1 = Option A).

Cut per-iteration token cost during quiet phases by returning a minimal `{changed: false, current_phase, status, phase_elapsed_seconds}` envelope on timeout and by skipping the 10-message `recent_messages` fetch on the timeout path (HITL decision-3 + decision-6).
Prevent stuck-on-same-event races by threading a caller-supplied `since` cursor (last event ID from the prior call) into both the EventBus subscribe and the message_store long-poll (HITL decision-4).
Prevent self-waking on host-originated decision resolution by filtering `DECISION_RESOLVED` out of the trigger set (HITL decision-7).
Add a sibling `egg_inflight_host_waits` metric so operators can distinguish host-side waits from sandbox-side long-polls in the Waitress thread budget (refine-phase feedback).

Call out the `EGG_ORCH_WAITRESS_THREADS=16` budget explicitly in docs and decide whether to raise the default — one in-flight host wait per concurrent SDLC session sits on top of every existing sandbox-side `message wait-loop` (refine-phase feedback).
non_goals: Raising GET_STATUS_MAX_WAIT above 25s (blocked upstream by anthropics/claude-code#20335; refine-phase analysis and issue body both declare out of scope).

Replacing the polling loop with a persistent SSE connection (Option C was rejected at HITL decision-1 because streamable-HTTP MCP does not support streaming tool responses — mcp_server.py:159-176 returns a single JSON string per tool call).
Retrofitting `get_status` itself with event-driven wait (Option B rejected at HITL decision-1 — would affect non-SDLC consumers and break tests that assert wait ≈ 25s).
Any client-side dashboard hashing or canonical-diff logic in the SDLC prompt (Option D rejected at HITL decision-1 — LLM-level hashing is fragile).

Emitting OVERSEER_ALERT or CONSENSUS_* onto the EventBus, or emitting phase/decision/terminal events onto the message bus (HITL decision-5 keeps the two event sources as-is — we compose, we do not migrate).

Exposing `wait_for_status_change` over the Python SDK MCP tool surface (deferred in refine — HITL feedback said 'not sure / skip — defer to plan phase'; this plan recommends **streamable-HTTP only** for v1 and explicitly documents the Python SDK path as a follow-up if/when it ships).
Changing the SDLC skill's OVERSEER_ALERT deduplication logic (skills/sdlc/SKILL.md:397 — client-side dedup on message UUIDs is complementary to the new server-side wake and stays as-is).

host_polling_call_site.phase3_monitor_loop: lines 313-347 (§Phase 3 — Monitor). Step 1 at 317-319 instructs first poll → `get_status(task_id)` and subsequent polls → `get_status(task_id, wait=25)`. Closing reminder at 347 tells the LLM not to add a separate sleep.
host_polling_call_site.phase_s5_monitor_loop: lines 1182-1214 (§Phase S5 — Monitor). Same pattern — step 1 at 1186-1188 mirrors Phase 3.
host_polling_call_site.no_separate_mcp_reference_section: SKILL.md does NOT have a 'MCP Tools Reference' section (verified via grep — only prose-embedded tool usage). Prompt edits are localized to the two step-1 blocks above.
host_polling_call_site.oversight_alert_handling: lines 369-397. Client-side dedup keyed on message `id` (UUID). Remains complementary to the new server-side wake.

host_mcp_tool_path.get_status_wait_implementation: orchestrator/mcp_server.py:50-67 (`_apply_get_status_wait`): pops `wait` kwarg, awaits `asyncio.sleep(min(wait, GET_STATUS_MAX_WAIT))`. Runs BEFORE the sync handler via `await _apply_get_status_wait(tool_name, kwargs)` at line 171. Uses asyncio.sleep (not time.sleep) so no anyio worker thread is pinned during the wait.
host_mcp_tool_path.max_wait_constant: orchestrator/mcp_server.py:42 — `GET_STATUS_MAX_WAIT = 25`. Comment at lines 38-41 cites anthropics/claude-code#20335.
host_mcp_tool_path.status_envelope_builder: orchestrator/mcp_tools.py:1548-1655 (`_handle_get_status`). Shape: `{current_phase, status, pipeline:{id,repo,issue_number,created_at,pr_url?,pr_number?}, running_agents, completed_agents, phase_started_at, phase_elapsed_seconds, pending_decisions, recent_messages}`. Fetches `/api/v1/pipelines/{id}` (line 1563) then `/api/v1/pipelines/{id}/messages?limit=10` (line 1637).
host_mcp_tool_path.no_existing_helper: The `_handle_get_status` method IS the envelope builder; there is no separate factory function. New tool handler will either reuse `_handle_get_status` (full envelope on `changed: true`) or build the minimal envelope inline.

event_bus_primitive.eventbus_class: lines 119-317. Handlers stored in `_handlers: dict[EventType, list[EventHandler]]` and `_wildcard_handlers: list[EventHandler]`. Thread-safe via `threading.RLock`. `async_delivery=True` for the singleton (line 332).
event_bus_primitive.subscribe_api: lines 188-207 — `subscribe(event_type: EventType|None, handler: EventHandler)`. Synchronous callback model; handler is invoked on the delivery thread (async worker or caller thread).
event_bus_primitive.publish_and_emit: lines 228-276 — `publish(event)` and `emit(event_type, pipeline_id, data, source)`. Global helpers `get_event_bus()` and `emit_event(...)` at lines 324-353.
event_types_relevant_to_host: EventType.PIPELINE_CANCELLED ('pipeline.cancelled') — add this to the trigger set (SDLC treats cancel as terminal)
event_bus_primitive.emission_sites: orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py:513-553 wraps `report_pipeline_status` emissions via `_emit_pipeline_event`. DECISION_CREATED at line 11039. DECISION_RESOLVED at orchestrator/routes/decisions.py:450.
event_bus_primitive.missing_primitive: EventBus has no native async/await wait primitive. SSEClientManager (orchestrator/sse.py:111-300) solves this with a per-client Queue, subscribing a wildcard handler that puts events onto the queue. The new route will follow the same per-caller Queue pattern (bounded, short-lived).

message_store_long_poll_primitive.existing_route: orchestrator/routes/messages.py:347-436 (`GET /api/v1/pipelines/<id>/messages/wait`). Query params: `for` (repeatable, required message types), `role`, `from`, `since_id`, `timeout`, `limit`. Calls `message_store.get_messages(..., wait=timeout, wait_for_types=[...], from_role=..., from_tip=since_id is None)`.
message_store_long_poll_primitive.message_store_contract: orchestrator/message_store.py:180-222 (in-memory) + orchestrator/redis_message_store.py:158-240+ (Redis XREAD BLOCK). `from_tip=True` → only events arriving AFTER the call unblock the wait (issue #1925 fix). Caller passes `since_id` to override and resume from a cursor.
message_store_long_poll_primitive.in_flight_gauge: orchestrator/routes/messages.py:73-101 — `egg_inflight_long_polls` label `{endpoint: 'messages'}`. `_track_long_poll_start/_end` wraps the blocking call.
message_store_long_poll_primitive.metrics_pattern: Register gauge via `get_metrics_registry().gauge('egg_inflight_long_polls', labels={...})`; inc on entry, dec on exit (finally block).

waitress_thread_budget.min_refuse_to_boot: 4 → sys.exit(78) EX_CONFIG if operator sets below. Rationale in env_config.py:92-101.
waitress_thread_budget.channel_timeout: `max(EGG_MESSAGE_POLL_MAX_WAIT * 2 + 30, 120)` seconds (cli.py:309). Must exceed any single blocking read.
waitress_thread_budget.note: Sandbox-side waits already use part of this budget via `/messages/wait`. Adding one host-side wait per concurrent SDLC session on top of sandbox waits may pressure the 16-thread default under heavy concurrent-mode workloads — hence the refine-phase feedback to raise default or document cap.

provide_input_path.risk_if_not_filtered: A user-facing provide_input call from the same Claude session would self-wake the monitor loop — dashboard re-renders immediately, showing a now-empty pending_decisions list. Wastes a round-trip but is not a correctness bug.
provide_input_path.mitigation: Filter DECISION_RESOLVED out of the EventBus trigger set (HITL decision-7); additionally the `since` cursor (decision-4) prevents any event older than the last wake from re-firing.

key_constraints: GET_STATUS_MAX_WAIT = 25s is immutable in this scope (anthropics/claude-code#20335 ignores MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT on streamable-HTTP transport). The new tool must share this cap but expose it as a single constant so a future upstream fix is a one-line change.
FastMCP tool registration is schema-driven (orchestrator/mcp_tools.py:64 PIPELINE_TOOLS list). New tool must follow the existing shape so it lights up automatically across mcp_server.py:199-204.
Streamable-HTTP MCP returns a single JSON string per tool call (mcp_server.py:176). No streaming/SSE chunking possible at the tool-call layer.

EventBus handlers are invoked synchronously on the delivery thread — handlers MUST NOT block, otherwise they starve other subscribers. The new wait endpoint's EventBus handler must be a thin `queue.put_nowait` adapter.

message_store.get_messages(wait=timeout) runs on a waitress worker thread and blocks that thread for up to `timeout` seconds. The new endpoint holds one waitress thread per in-flight caller — MUST be metered via `egg_inflight_host_waits`.

from_tip=True is the correct default when the caller did not pass `since_id`; this is the #1925 fix. The new tool's `since` parameter maps directly to `since_id` on the message_store call and to a cursor comparison on the EventBus queue.

Backend parity: the in-memory message store (default in CI) uses `threading.Condition`; the Redis store uses `XREAD BLOCK`. Both already support `wait_for_types` with from_tip semantics — no new store work.
Waitress channel_timeout must stay > any single blocking call (currently `2 * EGG_MESSAGE_POLL_MAX_WAIT + 30s`). The new 25s cap is well inside this.
Host MCP path does NOT traverse the Squid gateway (verified in refine analysis). Gateway timeouts are not in the host path; Waitress channel_timeout is the only relevant socket cap.

The SDLC skill is the contract — prompt edits at skills/sdlc/SKILL.md:317-319 (Phase 3 step 1) and skills/sdlc/SKILL.md:1186-1188 (Phase S5 step 1) are the only user-facing surface changes. No separate 'MCP Tools Reference' section exists.
DECISION_RESOLVED MUST be excluded from the EventBus trigger set (HITL decision-7). DECISION_CREATED is included.

PIPELINE_CANCELLED MUST be included as a terminal trigger (treated as 'done' by Phase 3 / Phase S5) even though the refine analysis only enumerated COMPLETED/FAILED — the SDLC skill already maps cancel to exit.

The 10-message `recent_messages` fetch on `_handle_get_status` line 1637 MUST be skipped on the timeout path (HITL decision-6). On the `changed: true` path the full envelope (including recent_messages) is returned, matching current behaviour.

OVERSEER_ALERT message UUIDs must remain visible to the SDLC skill on the `changed: true` path so its existing dedup (skills/sdlc/SKILL.md:397) keeps working. Returning the full envelope on `changed: true` satisfies this.
File boundaries (plan phase): architect writes only to `.egg-state/agent-outputs/1932-architect-output.json`. No production-code edits in this phase.

option_A_sibling_mcp_tool.summary: New `wait_for_status_change(task_id, wait=25, since=...)` MCP tool alongside the unchanged `get_status`.
pros: Clean separation — get_status stays a pure status read; wait_for_status_change is the event wake.
Opt-in: non-SDLC callers (babysit-pr internal, agent-diagnose, external MCP consumers) keep current behavior — zero breakage risk.
Minimal-envelope timeout path is an explicit contract — the SDLC skill can cheaply skip dashboard re-render on `changed: false`.
Mirrors the in-sandbox `message wait` / `wait-loop` idiom users already know (docs/reference/agent-wait-patterns.md).
Pairs naturally with a `since` cursor — parameter is visible in the tool signature instead of being a hidden get_status side-effect.
cons: Adds one tool entry to the MCP surface (schema + handler + tests + docs).
SDLC prompt must branch on 'first poll' vs 'subsequent poll' — minor LLM-drift risk at the boundary.
Two polling primitives that look superficially similar; future authors must choose.

option_B_retrofit_get_status.summary: Add event-driven wait to existing `get_status(wait=25)` — no new tool.
cons: Behavior change to a widely-used tool — babysit-pr and external consumers observe earlier returns.
No room for the minimal no-change envelope without either adding an `events_only: bool` flag (still a semantic change) or always emitting full envelope (defeats HITL decision-3).
Tests that assert wait ≈ 25s would break (orchestrator/tests/test_mcp_tools.py ~1028).
Stateless streamable-HTTP transport has no natural home for the `since` cursor.

option_C_sse_consumption.summary: Persistent SSE consumption via a `stream_pipeline` MCP tool.
pros: Fully event-driven, reuses existing orchestrator/sse.py infrastructure.
cons: Streamable-HTTP MCP returns a single JSON string per call (mcp_server.py:176) — no way to stream chunks back to the host.
Would require a different transport or a polling adapter; conceptually this is no longer 'the host-side counterpart of #1919'.

option_D_client_side_hash.summary: Shorter polls (wait=5) plus LLM-level dashboard hashing to skip re-renders.
cons: Still burns tokens on 5s cadence during quiet phases — defeats the issue.
LLM-level hashing is unreliable; defeats issue intent.

recommended_approach.headline: Ship Option A — a new `wait_for_status_change` MCP tool that composes the existing EventBus and message_store long-poll, returns early on any trigger event with the full get_status envelope, and returns a minimal `{changed: false, current_phase, status, phase_elapsed_seconds, cursor}` envelope on 25s timeout. The SDLC skill's Phase 3 and Phase S5 monitor loops replace `get_status(task_id, wait=25)` with `wait_for_status_change(task_id, wait=25, since=<last_cursor>)`.
why_this_shape: Every HITL decision and every refine-phase feedback item maps to a concrete element of this design — no deferrals beyond the two items the refine phase explicitly punted.
Reuses the two existing server primitives (EventBus pub/sub, message_store.get_messages with wait_for_types + from_tip) — no new storage or cursor semantics.
Keeps the change additive: get_status is untouched, no migration risk, no behavior change for non-SDLC callers.
Fits the Waitress thread budget exactly the way `/messages/wait` does today (one thread per wait), with a sibling `egg_inflight_host_waits` metric so operators can see the host-side load separately.

Parameterizing GET_STATUS_MAX_WAIT behind a single constant makes raising the 25s cap a one-line change if anthropics/claude-code#20335 ever lifts — addresses the refine-phase feedback 'Keep design flexible'.

tool_signature.name: wait_for_status_change

wait.description: Seconds to block waiting for the next pipeline-relevant event. Capped at GET_STATUS_MAX_WAIT (25s).

since.description: Optional cursor from the prior call's response (`cursor` field). When set, events older than this cursor do not wake the wait. When absent, from_tip=True semantics apply (only events arriving AFTER the call can wake).

tool_signature.response_changed_true: Full get_status envelope (identical shape to current `_handle_get_status` return) plus `changed: true` and `cursor: <id>` (the event ID that woke the wait; host passes this as `since` on the next call).
tool_signature.response_changed_false: Minimal `{changed: false, current_phase, status, phase_elapsed_seconds, cursor: <id>}` — `cursor` is the last-known event ID at wake-up so the host can resume. NO `recent_messages` fetch (HITL decision-6).

eventbus_exclude: Agent-lifecycle events (AGENT_STARTED, AGENT_COMPLETED) — out of scope per decision-2 'Issue-as-written'
message_bus_exclude: CONSENSUS_ACK, CONSENSUS_WITHDRAW — HITL decision-2 picked 'Issue-as-written', not 'Maximal'

cursor_semantics.encoding: An opaque string that encodes both the last-seen message_store stream ID (e.g. Redis '1700000000000-0' or in-memory integer index) and the last-seen EventBus event sequence. Recommended concrete encoding: `'{msg_id}|{event_seq}'` with base64 wrapping so hosts treat it as opaque.
cursor_semantics.server_parse: On entry, split cursor into `msg_since_id` (passed to message_store.get_messages) and `event_since_seq` (compared against EventBus per-pipeline monotonic counter — NEW: add a counter on EventBus or route it through a per-pipeline deque+lock in the new route's helper).
cursor_semantics.response_cursor: Always include `cursor` in both changed:true and changed:false responses. On changed:true cursor = ID of the triggering event. On changed:false cursor = max(msg_tip_id, event_tip_seq) at wake time.
cursor_semantics.fallback_when_absent: If the caller omits `since`, the new route passes `from_tip=True` to message_store.get_messages AND seeds `event_since_seq = current_tip` before subscribing to EventBus — both sources start 'tip' per #1925.

concurrency_and_threading.route_shape: New HTTP route `GET /api/v1/pipelines/<id>/status/wait` in orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py (co-located with /stream so the event-bus helper cache in pipelines.py is reused). The tool handler `_handle_wait_for_status_change` in mcp_tools.py does: (1) seed `cursor` from caller's `since`; (2) call new route; (3) if response says changed: call existing `_handle_get_status` and merge its envelope with `{changed: true, cursor}`; (4) if timeout: return minimal envelope.
concurrency_and_threading.route_internals: Create a short-lived `queue.Queue(maxsize=16)` per caller. Subscribe a wildcard handler (filtered by pipeline_id + event_type ∈ trigger_set + event_seq > event_since_seq) that does `q.put_nowait(('event', event))`. Spawn a daemon Thread that calls `message_store.get_messages(wait=25, wait_for_types=[...], since_id=msg_since_id, from_tip=msg_since_id is None)` and puts `('msg', msgs)` on the same queue when it returns. Main thread does `q.get(timeout=25)` — first source wins. On return: unsubscribe handler, signal message_store thread to stop (best effort — it will return on its own within 25s), return the matched source.
concurrency_and_threading.thread_safety: EventBus handler runs on delivery thread, which is either the caller of emit_event() or the EventBus worker thread. Using queue.Queue guarantees the main-thread wake is safe. Unsubscribe is already RLock-safe (events.py:199-207).
concurrency_and_threading.waitress_thread_pressure: One route call = one waitress worker thread blocked + one daemon thread running message_store.get_messages. Same pattern as existing /messages/wait (which holds one waitress thread). The daemon message_store thread is a SECOND thread per call — document this and raise EGG_ORCH_WAITRESS_THREADS default OR budget for it. See RISK-3 below.
concurrency_and_threading.alternative_simpler_implementation: If the daemon-thread cost is judged too high, we can instead use asyncio-friendly wait by moving the route to a quart/asgi path — but the whole orchestrator is Flask+Waitress today and introducing asyncio just for this route is out of proportion. Daemon-thread model matches /messages/wait.

minimal_envelope.compute: Single cheap `/api/v1/pipelines/{id}` fetch at entry OR cached-on-EventBus-tip — recommend fetching once on entry (before subscribing) so the envelope reflects current state. Skip the 10-message `recent_messages` enrichment (saves one HTTP round-trip per timeout, HITL decision-6).

skill_prompt_changes.phase_3_step_1_replacement: Replace skills/sdlc/SKILL.md:317-319 with: `1. Call the \`wait_for_status_change\` MCP tool with the \`task_id\` and the cursor from the prior response. First poll after submission: \`get_status(task_id)\` (no wait). Subsequent polls: \`wait_for_status_change(task_id, wait=25, since=<last_cursor>)\`. The tool returns immediately when a pipeline-relevant event fires (OVERSEER_ALERT, pending decision, phase transition, consensus state change, terminal state) or after 25s with a minimal no-change payload.`
skill_prompt_changes.phase_3_step_1_branch: Add step 1a: `If response.changed is false, skip dashboard re-render and go straight back to step 1 with the new cursor. If changed is true, proceed to step 2 (dashboard render).`
skill_prompt_changes.closing_reminder_update: Line 347 / 1214 — replace 'The `wait` parameter on `get_status` handles the polling delay internally' with 'The `wait` parameter on `wait_for_status_change` blocks the server-side event loop and returns early on any pipeline-relevant event. Do not use separate sleep commands.'

metric_and_budget.new_metric: `egg_inflight_host_waits` gauge with labels `{endpoint: 'pipelines.status_wait'}`. Registered in orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py near the new route, incremented before the queue.get, decremented in finally.
metric_and_budget.waitress_default: Recommend raising EGG_ORCH_WAITRESS_THREADS default from 16 to 24 in env_config.py (one host-side wait per concurrent SDLC session on top of sandbox loads). Document the budget explicitly in docs/reference/agent-wait-patterns.md §7 and docs/architecture/orchestrator.md. Keep the refuse-to-boot floor at 4.

deferred_items_resolved.python_sdk_surface: Recommend v1 ships streamable-HTTP ONLY (not the PR #1920 Python SDK MCP surface). Rationale: only the SDLC skill needs it, and the Python SDK MCP is for in-sandbox agents that already use `egg-orch message wait-loop`. Follow-up issue can expose it to the Python SDK if a need arises.
deferred_items_resolved.60s_liveness_floor: Recommend interpreting the floor as **aspirational** (cap single call at 25s; rely on SDLC loop composition for aggregate quiet interval). The SDLC loop re-issues wait_for_status_change within ~100ms of each return, so two back-to-back 25s timeouts + one LLM turn ≤ 55s << 60s aspirational floor. No separate liveness mechanism needed. Document this in docs/reference/agent-wait-patterns.md.

C1_eventbus_sequence_counter.change: Add a per-pipeline monotonic sequence counter so the new route can reject events older than the caller's `since` cursor. Minimal surface: `_event_seq: dict[str, int]` on EventBus, incremented inside `publish()` and exposed on the Event dataclass as `sequence: int`.
C1_eventbus_sequence_counter.size: ~30 lines; no behavior change for existing consumers (new field defaults to 0 if sequence ordering is unneeded).
C1_eventbus_sequence_counter.alternative: Skip this and rely on per-pipeline deque-with-ID in the route's helper. Simpler but less reusable. Leave the final decision to task_planner.

C2_new_orchestrator_route.new_route: `GET /api/v1/pipelines/<pipeline_id>/status/wait` — query params: `wait` (default 25, clamped to GET_STATUS_MAX_WAIT), `since` (opaque cursor).
C2_new_orchestrator_route.behavior: Parse cursor → seed `msg_since_id` + `event_since_seq`. Create per-call `queue.Queue(maxsize=16)`. Subscribe a wildcard handler filtered by (pipeline_id, event_type ∈ trigger_set, sequence > event_since_seq) that queues `('event', event)`. Spawn daemon thread calling `message_store.get_messages(wait=timeout, wait_for_types=[OVERSEER_ALERT, CONSENSUS_*], since_id=msg_since_id, from_tip=msg_since_id is None)` and queues `('msg', msgs)` on return. Main thread does `q.get(timeout=timeout)`. On event: unsubscribe, return `{changed: true, trigger: 'event', event: {...}, cursor: <event_id>}`. On msg: unsubscribe, return `{changed: true, trigger: 'message', messages: [...], cursor: <msg_id>}`. On timeout (queue.Empty): unsubscribe, fetch current pipeline state via existing helper, return `{changed: false, current_phase, status, phase_elapsed_seconds, cursor: <current_tip_cursor>}`.
C2_new_orchestrator_route.file_boundaries: Does NOT need pipeline state-branch access — only reads message_store + EventBus + single pipeline snapshot.

C3_new_mcp_tool_handler.schema_entry: New PIPELINE_TOOLS entry named `wait_for_status_change` at a sensible spot (next to `get_status`, ~line 305). inputSchema as described in recommended_approach.tool_signature.
C3_new_mcp_tool_handler.handler: `_handle_wait_for_status_change(self, args)` at a method near `_handle_get_status`. Calls `self._make_request(f'/api/v1/pipelines/{task_id}/status/wait?wait={wait}&since={since or ""}', method='GET')`. On changed: merge with `_handle_get_status` call OR construct from event data. On not-changed: return route's payload verbatim.
C3_new_mcp_tool_handler.wait_injection_in_mcp_server: orchestrator/mcp_server.py:50-67 `_apply_get_status_wait` currently checks `if tool_name != 'get_status': return`. RECOMMENDATION: do NOT apply the async sleep wrapper to `wait_for_status_change` — the wait is already applied server-side inside the route's blocking call, so the async-sleep wrapper would double the delay. Generalize the check or (simpler) leave `_apply_get_status_wait` as-is and do not register the wait behavior for the new tool.

edits: Lines 317-319 (Phase 3 step 1) — replace get_status(wait=25) with wait_for_status_change(wait=25, since=...)
Add a new short section after Phase 3 step 1 — 'Cursor handling' — showing how to thread `cursor` from one response to the next `since`.

technical_decisions.decision: New sibling tool `wait_for_status_change` instead of retrofitting get_status.
technical_decisions.justification: HITL decision-1 (Option A). Avoids non-SDLC regression, enables the minimal-envelope contract, and matches the in-sandbox wait-loop idiom.
technical_decisions.alternative_rejected: Retrofit get_status (Option B) — breaks get_status behavior for external consumers, blocks the minimal-envelope path.

technical_decisions.decision: Trigger set = Issue-as-written (OVERSEER_ALERT, DECISION_CREATED, terminal, phase transitions, consensus state changes).
technical_decisions.justification: HITL decision-2. Balances completeness against wake-storm risk from including every BRC per-message event.
technical_decisions.alternative_rejected: Maximal (adds CONSENSUS_PROPOSE + AGENT_FAILED + AGENT_TIMEOUT + heartbeat gaps) — would wake the host on internal plumbing events that don't require user action.

technical_decisions.decision: Minimal no-change envelope on timeout `{changed: false, current_phase, status, phase_elapsed_seconds, cursor}`.
technical_decisions.justification: HITL decision-3. Cheap dashboard re-render — the SDLC skill branches on `changed` and goes straight back to the next wait call.
technical_decisions.alternative_rejected: Full envelope on every timeout — zero prompt churn but wastes the optimization; Hybrid first-call-full — unnecessary state.

technical_decisions.justification: HITL decision-4. Eliminates the stuck-on-same-event race cleanly without introducing server-side session state.
technical_decisions.alternative_rejected: from_tip=True only — leaves a transition-race window when the host switches from get_status to wait_for_status_change between phases; Auto-session — adds state to a stateless transport.

technical_decisions.decision: Both EventBus AND message_store long-poll (composed in the new route).
technical_decisions.justification: HITL decision-5. Events live in their natural source — phase/decision/terminal on EventBus, OVERSEER_ALERT/CONSENSUS_* on the message bus. Migrating either is out of scope.

technical_decisions.decision: Skip recent_messages fetch on the timeout path.
technical_decisions.justification: HITL decision-6. Saves one HTTP round-trip per quiet cycle. OVERSEER_ALERT / CONSENSUS_* messages would not be new anyway (if they were, the wait would have returned early).
technical_decisions.alternative_rejected: Keep on every poll — defeats part of the token-saving goal.

technical_decisions.decision: Filter DECISION_RESOLVED out of the EventBus trigger set.
technical_decisions.justification: HITL decision-7. Prevents the host's own provide_input calls from self-waking the monitor loop.
technical_decisions.alternative_rejected: Rely on since_event_id cursor alone — works but leaves a self-wake window in the race between `provide_input` returning and the next wait call.

technical_decisions.decision: Streamable-HTTP MCP surface only for v1 (not Python SDK MCP).
technical_decisions.justification: Refine-phase feedback deferred to plan. Only the SDLC skill needs host-side event waits; Python SDK MCP is for in-sandbox agents which use `egg-orch message wait-loop`. Narrower blast radius.
technical_decisions.follow_up: Revisit when/if PR #1920 ships and a non-SDLC Python-SDK consumer emerges.

technical_decisions.decision: 60s liveness floor is aspirational, not literal.
technical_decisions.justification: Refine-phase feedback deferred to plan. Each call is capped at 25s + ~100ms LLM-turn gap; two back-to-back timeouts ≤ 55s. Adding a separate liveness timer duplicates what the loop composition already guarantees.
technical_decisions.follow_up: If operators report pipelines going silent for >60s in the field, add a health-check hitting GET /health from the overseer.

technical_decisions.justification: Refine-phase feedback: 'Raise default or document cap in plan. Call out the budget risk explicitly.' One host-side wait per active SDLC session stacks on existing sandbox-side waits; 24 leaves headroom for ~8 concurrent SDLC sessions + 16 sandbox waits.
technical_decisions.alternative_rejected: Leave at 16 and document — operators already set this in prod; bumping the default is a safer fail-forward.

technical_decisions.decision: Parameterize GET_STATUS_MAX_WAIT as the sole knob, shared with the new tool.
technical_decisions.justification: Refine-phase feedback: 'Keep design flexible in case it lifts'. If anthropics/claude-code#20335 is fixed upstream, one const change unlocks both tools.
technical_decisions.alternative_rejected: Separate constant per tool — doubles the future edit surface.

technical_decisions.justification: Refine-phase feedback — operators need to distinguish host-side from sandbox-side waits in alerting.
technical_decisions.alternative_rejected: Reuse `egg_inflight_long_polls` with a new label — loses existing alert thresholds that assume messages.py as the only source.

open_questions_for_task_planner_and_revi: Should cursor encoding be `base64(json({msg_id, event_seq}))` (explicit, self-documenting, larger payload) or `f'{msg_id}|{event_seq}'` (compact, opaque)? Task planner to pick — either works.

Should the EventBus per-pipeline sequence counter (component C1) land in this issue or be replaced with a route-local per-caller deque+lock? Route-local is simpler but couples the route to EventBus internals; global counter on EventBus is more reusable but touches a widely-used class.

For the daemon-thread that blocks on message_store.get_messages, is there a clean way to cancel it early when the EventBus fires first? Current plan: let it run to completion (≤25s, same cap) — acceptable since the next call will consume its messages via the cursor. Task planner: confirm this is acceptable or propose a shutdown channel.

Should the minimal envelope on timeout include `pending_decisions_count: <int>` so the skill can detect a HITL gate during a quiet phase without waiting for the DECISION_CREATED event? Current plan: NO, because DECISION_CREATED already fires; include only if task planner sees a race.

Should the wait_for_status_change error path (e.g. pipeline not found, cursor malformed) return a 400/404 with an error body, or a 200 with `{changed: false, error: ...}`? Recommend 400/404 for parity with other routes — task planner to confirm.

risks_for_risk_analyst.title: Stuck-on-same-event race during get_status → wait_for_status_change handoff
risks_for_risk_analyst.description: On the very first wait_for_status_change call after a phase transition, `since` may not yet be set; an event that fired between get_status returning and wait_for_status_change entering would be missed (from_tip=True) or re-fire every call (from_tip=False).
risks_for_risk_analyst.mitigation: HITL decision-4 `since` cursor. First call uses `since=None` → from_tip semantics. Subsequent calls carry the cursor from the prior response. SDLC prompt must include cursor in the very first wait call after the initial get_status.
risks_for_risk_analyst.residual: If the SDLC prompt LLM drifts and forgets to pass `since`, we lose events. Mitigated by a server-side 'best-effort tip' when missing — correct for steady state, acceptable for edge.

risks_for_risk_analyst.title: Host-originated provide_input self-wakes the monitor loop
risks_for_risk_analyst.description: The user answers a HITL decision via provide_input → DECISION_RESOLVED fires → would wake the current wait_for_status_change call if not filtered.
risks_for_risk_analyst.mitigation: HITL decision-7: filter DECISION_RESOLVED out of EventBus trigger set.
risks_for_risk_analyst.residual: Zero — filter is server-side and deterministic.

risks_for_risk_analyst.title: Waitress thread budget exhaustion under concurrent-mode load
risks_for_risk_analyst.description: Each wait_for_status_change holds one waitress worker thread (main) + spawns one daemon thread (message_store blocker). With 16 threads default and N concurrent SDLC sessions + sandbox long-polls, the pool can saturate.
risks_for_risk_analyst.mitigation: Component C6 — raise default from 16 to 24. Add `egg_inflight_host_waits` metric. Document the budget in docs/reference/agent-wait-patterns.md §7.
risks_for_risk_analyst.residual: Large deployments must still tune EGG_ORCH_WAITRESS_THREADS; refuse-to-boot floor protects against catastrophic under-provisioning.

risks_for_risk_analyst.title: Daemon thread leak if message_store blocker does not terminate on unsubscribe
risks_for_risk_analyst.description: When the main thread exits on event wake, the daemon message_store thread continues to block for the remaining wait. Acceptable but must not accumulate threads on rapid-turnover calls.
risks_for_risk_analyst.mitigation: Daemon thread is time-bounded (≤25s). Verify in test_pipelines_status_wait_route.py that the thread exits within wait+epsilon. Consider an in-memory `wait_cancel_event` threading.Event checked inside the store's inner loop — deferred unless tests show leak.
risks_for_risk_analyst.residual: Low — thread lifetime is bounded by the 25s cap.

risks_for_risk_analyst.title: Backend parity drift (in-memory vs Redis)
risks_for_risk_analyst.description: In-memory backend uses threading.Condition; Redis uses XREAD BLOCK. Both already support wait_for_types + from_tip, but cursor representation differs (integer index vs stream ID).
risks_for_risk_analyst.mitigation: Encode cursor as opaque string; decode per-backend inside the new route using `message_store.parse_cursor(cursor)` (add helper if not present). Unit tests cover both backends via parametrize.
risks_for_risk_analyst.residual: Existing pattern from /messages/wait works; copy-paste risk only.

risks_for_risk_analyst.title: EventBus handler blocks delivery thread
risks_for_risk_analyst.description: If the wildcard handler registered by the new route does anything expensive (state-store fetch, serialization), it blocks delivery for ALL other subscribers on the same EventBus worker thread.
risks_for_risk_analyst.mitigation: Handler is strictly `queue.put_nowait((event_type, event))` — trivial, non-blocking. Queue.Full is handled as a dropped event (log.warning, do not raise — the next publish will get through).
risks_for_risk_analyst.residual: Zero with correct implementation; tests must assert handler call latency ≤ 1ms.

risks_for_risk_analyst.title: Double-sleep bug if _apply_get_status_wait is accidentally applied to the new tool
risks_for_risk_analyst.description: The async-sleep wrapper at mcp_server.py:50-67 currently short-circuits on `tool_name != 'get_status'`. If a future author generalizes that check, wait_for_status_change would sleep 25s in the async wrapper AND another 25s in the server-side queue.get.
risks_for_risk_analyst.mitigation: Leave the `tool_name != 'get_status'` guard strict (explicit allow-list). Add a regression test that asserts the new tool's async wrapper does NOT sleep.

risks_for_risk_analyst.title: SKILL.md drift causes LLM to call the old get_status(wait=25) path anyway
risks_for_risk_analyst.description: Phase 3 and Phase S5 are long sections; partial edits can leave stale references to `get_status(wait=25)` elsewhere in the file (e.g. OVERSEER_ALERT handling refers to status fields, §Consensus Monitoring mentions get_status twice).
risks_for_risk_analyst.mitigation: Component C4 grep for every `get_status(` occurrence (~10 sites) and rewrite the polling ones. Non-polling sites (first poll, snapshot fallback) keep get_status. Review task must explicitly check grep output is empty for `get_status(task_id, wait=`.

risks_for_risk_analyst.title: OVERSEER_ALERT dedup duplication
risks_for_risk_analyst.description: Server-side filter will wake on any new OVERSEER_ALERT; client-side dedup (SKILL.md:397) also guards against re-prompt. If the two disagree on what 'new' means (e.g. server uses stream ID, client uses message UUID), double-prompts or missed prompts can occur.
risks_for_risk_analyst.mitigation: Server filter uses from_tip + since_id (stream ID); client still keys on UUID. The two are complementary, not conflicting — server decides 'is there a new alert' (efficiency), client decides 'should I prompt' (deduplication). Document this in SKILL.md §Overseer Alert Detection and test in integration_tests.
risks_for_risk_analyst.residual: Low — clarify in prompt + integration test.

risks_for_risk_analyst.title: Pipeline not found / cursor malformed
risks_for_risk_analyst.description: Caller passes a garbage cursor or a task_id that no longer exists; current error paths on /messages/wait return 400/404 but the new tool could mask this as `changed: false`.
risks_for_risk_analyst.mitigation: Return 400 on cursor parse failure (reject the cursor, caller can retry without `since`). Return 404 on missing pipeline. Tool handler surfaces the error to the skill, which falls back to get_status(task_id).
risks_for_risk_analyst.residual: Explicit error handling; covered by unit tests.

risks_for_risk_analyst.title: EGG_ORCH_WAITRESS_THREADS default bump impacts memory footprint
risks_for_risk_analyst.description: Raising default from 16 to 24 costs ~8 × waitress-thread-stack (default 512KB → ~4MB extra RSS). Negligible on a dev machine; non-zero on k8s deploys with tight memory limits.
risks_for_risk_analyst.mitigation: Document the ~4MB overhead in docs/reference/agent-wait-patterns.md §7. Operators who have set EGG_ORCH_WAITRESS_THREADS explicitly are unaffected.
